title: Vercingetorix surrenders at Alesia
description: After the siege of Alesia, Vercingetorix surrenders to Julius Caesar.

title: The Spanish Armada is defeated
description: Elizabeth I's fleet and the weather break the Spanish invasion fleet.

title: Storming of the Bastille
description: Crowds storm the Bastille prison in Paris on 14 July.

title: Perry's black ships arrive
description: Commodore Perry's squadron arrives off Edo and demands that Japan open its ports.

title: Carmen opens at the Opéra-Comique
description: Bizet's opera gets a cool reception. Three months later he dies, aged 36.

fr.title: Carmen à l’Opéra-Comique
fr.description: L’opéra de Bizet reçoit un accueil froid. Trois mois plus tard, il meurt à 36 ans.

title: Cézanne and Zola meet at school
description: Cézanne and Zola become friends at the Collège Bourbon in Aix-en-Provence.

title: Charlemagne is crowned emperor
description: The pope crowns Charlemagne emperor in Rome on Christmas Day.

title: Churchill becomes prime minister
description: Churchill takes office in May 1940, as Germany invades France.

title: The court moves to Versailles
description: Louis XIV moves the royal court and government to Versailles.

title: Darwin is born
description: Charles Darwin is born in Shrewsbury on 12 February, the same day as Abraham Lincoln.

title: Christine de Pizan writes about Joan of Arc
description: Christine de Pizan writes a poem celebrating Joan of Arc, the only one written in Joan's lifetime.

title: The first Impressionist exhibition
description: Monet, Cézanne and Morisot show work at the first Impressionist exhibition in Paris.

fr.title: La première exposition impressionniste
fr.description: Monet, Cézanne et Morisot exposent à la première exposition impressionniste, à Paris.

title: Japan's first railway
description: Japan's first railway line opens between Shinbashi in Tokyo and the port of Yokohama.

title: The Tale of Genji is read at court
description: Murasaki Shikibu's diary records The Tale of Genji being read at the Heian court.

title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
description: Hokusai publishes the print, part of his Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.

title: Battle of Hastings
description: William of Normandy defeats Harold II and becomes king of England.

title: The Honnō-ji incident
description: Oda Nobunaga dies at Honnō-ji in Kyoto, betrayed by his general Akechi Mitsuhide.

title: Zola publishes “J'accuse…!”
description: Zola's open letter on the Dreyfus affair fills the front page of L'Aurore. Clemenceau, who wrote for the paper, gave it its headline.

title: Joan of Arc is burned at Rouen
description: Joan of Arc is tried for heresy and burned at the stake in Rouen.

title: Liberation of Paris
description: De Gaulle walks down the Champs-Élysées after the liberation of Paris.

title: Zola publishes L'Œuvre
description: Cézanne saw himself in the novel's failed painter, and the two old friends drifted apart.

title: Ada Lovelace's notes on the Analytical Engine
description: Her notes include an algorithm for Babbage's machine, often called the first computer program.

title: Marie Antoinette is guillotined
description: Marie Antoinette is executed in October, during the Reign of Terror.

title: The Meiji Restoration
description: Imperial rule is restored and Edo is renamed Tokyo.

title: Bashō sets out for the deep north
description: Bashō begins the journey he writes up as The Narrow Road to the Deep North.

title: On the Origin of Species
description: Darwin publishes his theory of evolution by natural selection.

title: Polonium and radium
description: Marie and Pierre Curie announce two new radioactive elements: polonium, named after her native Poland, and radium.

title: The People's Republic is proclaimed
description: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China in Beijing on 1 October.

title: Newton publishes the Principia
description: Newton sets out his laws of motion and universal gravitation.

title: Qin unifies China
description: The king of Qin conquers the last rival state and takes the title of first emperor.

title: Rashomon wins at Venice
description: Kurosawa's Rashomon wins the Golden Lion and introduces Japanese cinema to the world.

title: Sen no Rikyū is ordered to die
description: Hideyoshi orders his tea master, Sen no Rikyū, to take his own life.

title: Sakamoto Ryōma is assassinated
description: Sakamoto Ryōma is killed in Kyoto, weeks after the shogun hands power back to the emperor.

title: The last samurai revolt
description: Samurai led by Saigō Takamori rise against the new government in the Satsuma Rebellion, and are defeated.

title: Battle of Sekigahara
description: Tokugawa Ieyasu wins the battle that leads to 250 years of Tokugawa rule.

title: Shakespeare is born
description: William Shakespeare is born in Stratford-upon-Avon, the same year as Galileo.

title: Joan of Arc lifts the siege of Orléans
description: Aged about 17, Joan of Arc leads the force that ends the English siege of Orléans.

title: The Tokyo Olympics
description: Tokyo hosts the Olympics. The first Shinkansen line opened days before.

title: Zheng He's first voyage
description: Zheng He sails with the first of the Ming treasure fleets to the Indian Ocean.

title: France legalises abortion
description: The law legalising abortion, steered through parliament by Simone Veil, comes into force.

title: Wu Zetian rules in her own name
description: Wu Zetian proclaims her own dynasty and becomes China's only empress regnant.

title: Yoritomo becomes shogun
description: Minamoto no Yoritomo takes the title of shogun. Japan's warrior government begins.

title: Kublai Khan proclaims the Yuan dynasty
description: Kublai Khan gives his empire a Chinese dynastic name, the Yuan.
